basis: Bile duct paucity, cardiac defects and vertebral anomalies are diagnostic features; renal abnormalities occur in ~39%. Posterior embryotoxon usually causes no functional damage.
Defined by bone inflammation; the umbrella includes infectious and noninfectious causes, so no universal immune mechanism applies.
Inherited axonal motor and sensory peripheral neuropathy; weakness and muscle wasting reflect denervation.
Disorder of ocular accommodation caused by sustained accommodative spasm.
Gonadal dysgenesis can impair gonadal endocrine function and pubertal development; associated Turner features are not universal.
Inflammation of nasal mucosa; nose and upper airways belong to pulmonary. An allergic or infectious mechanism is not universal.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; retinal degeneration defines the disease.
Epileptic neurodevelopmental disease; cleft palate, strabismus and conductive hearing impairment each reported in 1/3. Tiny cohort; infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.
Congenital eyelid tarsal malformation causing entropion and possible corneal injury; tarsus here is part of the eyelid.
Autoimmune cerebellar dysfunction defines both the neurologic location and immune mechanism.
Squamous carcinoma arising in the esophagus; no common additional organ involvement is established.
Inherited skin fragility with blistering and nail dystrophy from BP230 deficiency; this is not autoimmune epidermolysis bullosa.
Disorder of phosphate homeostasis; skeletal or other organ damage is not universal across hypo- and hyperphosphatemic subtypes.
Congenital absence of teeth defines the disorder; teeth and associated oral clefts belong to gastrointestinal.
Phytanic acid disorder with defining retinal degeneration; neuropathy/ataxia and cardiomyopathy annotated 80-99%. Cap excludes common hearing, skin and skeletal involvement.
Severe skeletal dysplasia with short ribs and polydactyly; pulmonary hypoplasia affects most and causes lethal respiratory insufficiency.
Abnormal development and impaired renal tissue formation in one kidney define the disease.
Plasmalogen synthesis defect with defining rhizomelic skeletal dysplasia and cataracts; severe developmental impairment occurs in most patients.
Iodine-related thyroid hormone deficiency; an autoimmune mechanism is not inherent.
Congenital contractures with peripheral neuropathy; vocal cord paresis/respiratory failure and corneal scarring each reported in 1/1 assessed. Very small cohort.
BBS12 phenotype includes retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and common renal disease; developmental impairment occurs in >30%. Polydactyly omitted at cap.
The supplied definition explicitly requires organic brain damage from alcohol, supporting neurologic despite the psychiatric name.
Benign neoplasm arising from vascular tissue; a cutaneous location is not universal across the umbrella.
Bacterial infection defines the mechanism; no particular organ site is specified or established as commonly damaged.
Inherited brain iron accumulation disorder with developmental impairment and neurodegeneration; optic atrophy is occasional (5-29%), and eye movement abnormalities are neurologic.
